trust_decision.summary: Decided at httplib2/__init__.py:388-411 (_decompressContent): after the whole body has already been read, a response is inflated only when content-encoding is gzip or deflate, with no size, ratio or chunk bound; the published fix replaces both decoders with an incrementally-checked LimitDecoder (new httplib2/decode.py) whose limits are merged in Http.__init__ from constructor args, then httplib2_decode_limit_* env vars, then defaults.

landing_point.why: The only code in the tree that inflates a response body and the only caller of gzip.GzipFile / zlib.decompress on untrusted bytes; summary wording (unbounded gzip/deflate handling) points straight at this function.

fix_sites.entry_point: Http.request() (call site must now pass self.limit_kwargs)
fix_sites.module_kind: core package module, response read path

fix_sites.entry_point: Http(...) constructor and module import (try_value_or_env appended after httplib2/__init__.py:1802)
Http.request() via LimitDecoder/ZlibDecoder/DeflateDecoder; also exposed as httplib2.decode API

fix_sites.module_kind: packaging metadata (>=3.6 raised to >=3.8 for typing.Protocol)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The constructor/env-var limit plumbing is configuration, not the decompression vulnerability: the report's PoC only needs one default limit inside _decompressContent, so the Http(...) kwargs and httplib2_decode_limit_* merge can be argued to be a separate feature request.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate bodies must keep decompressing: content-encoding: deflate bodies that are zlib-encapsulated (the historic MAX_WBITS-then--MAX_WBITS fallback), and small highly-compressible bodies whose inflation ratio exceeds any fixed ratio. A rewrite that uses one strict wbits, or enforces the ratio unconditionally, rejects both.

O6_input_shapes: zlib-encapsulated stream (wbits 15): content-encoding: zlib newly accepted, and deflate bodies that are zlib-wrapped
raw deflate stream (wbits -15) via the fallback second decoder attempt
limit values as int/float from Http() and as strings from env vars, including 0 (falsy but meaningful) and chunk_size=0 meaning 'whole input'

O7_producer.where: httplib2/__init__.py:1229-1310 (merge implemented by fix.diff:229-243 and try_value_or_env at fix.diff:263-273)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cache FRESH return path that decompresses cached bodies when the disk cache keeps wire bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: storing inflated bodies bloats the FileCache, so a maintainer could plausibly store compressed bytes and inflate on read - a save/reload route the LimitDecoder check never sees.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: size-bounded streaming read of the response body before it is handed to the decoder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the memory peak is response.read(); a maintainer worried about memory could cap the socket read separately and still leave the inflate call unbounded.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second decoder for another advertised accept-encoding (br, zstd) reaching the same sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: compression support grows by advertising more encodings in accept-encoding, and each new decoder would need the same hard/safe/ratio bound.

O9_family: decompression bomb / uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-409 improper handling of highly compressed data; CWE-400, CWE-770)

O10_build.language: Python (3.6+ at pinned commit; fix raises to 3.8 for typing.Protocol)
O10_build.toolchain: setuptools/pip (setup.py, requirements.txt pyparsing>=3.1,<4); pytest configured in setup.cfg:13-27 with pytest-timeout/pytest-cov/pytest-randomly

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Inflate the whole body first (gzip.GzipFile(...).read() / zlib.decompress) and compare len(content) to a constant, keeping only the gzip branch - still allocates the bomb and drops the zlib-encapsulated deflate and the zlib encoding.
